**Group:** Diatoms  ·  **Optics:** high-mag, low-mag

## Defining characteristics

Cells are club-shaped (clavate): one end is expanded into a heavier "foot" while the other tapers into a long, fine trailing arm. The foot poles gather at a common centre so the colony radiates outward as a star or helix if chain is long. Key features: markedly unequal cell ends with club, central attachment, star or helical colony. Asterionellopsis glacialis (most common) and Asterionellopsis kariana.

## Distinguishing from similar classes

| Similar class | How to tell them apart |
|---|---|
| **thalassionema** | Asterionellopsis cells are clavate with a distinct foot at the colony centre. |
| **chaetoceros** | Chaetoceros cells are more rounded and rectangular, where Asterionellopsis is agnular. Setae (if visible) radiate from both side of the valve. |
